slides.title: Set the standard
slides.text: Today Set the standard Session 1 · Assurance proportionate to risk Four roles, business risk as effect and likelihood, and four assurance levels a peer can apply Session 2 · A team review checklist From a personal checklist to the unit's: adapt a published one, item by item, and tie each item to a level Session 3 · Reproducibility as a team rule Re-run before reading: the failures a re-run finds and the repository rules that prevent them Session 4 · Rules for AI-assisted analysis What an analyst verifies, discloses and keeps when an assistant drafts the work

slides.title: Twelve analysts, four sponsors, and no shared rule for checking
slides.text: The case Twelve analysts, four sponsors, and no shared rule for checking Ras Sahil Ports Authority : four terminals, marine pilots and tugs, a board that decides tariffs and capital The analytics unit serves marine operations, commercial affairs, finance and staffing Three senior analysts, six mid-level, three juniors More and more drafts start with Musawwada, the unit's drafting assistant You are Arjwan Al-Huqail Head of the unit. Your job is no longer to review one analysis well: it is to make every analysis reviewed well enough, by someone, on time.

slides.title: Assurance proportionate to risk
slides.text: Session 1 Assurance proportionate to risk Explain the four assurance roles and why the assurer is independent of the analyst Grade a request by the effect of an error and the complexity of the work Assign an assurance level with a matrix a peer applies the same way 01

slides.title: The errors readers found came from work checked too little for its use
slides.text: Last year's log The errors readers found came from work checked too little for its use 5 of 10 under-assured requests had an error found after release 1 of 20 of the others did "Under-assured": a lower level than the standard you write in Lab 1.1 requires A board paper on a fee change got a self-check; so did a public dwell statistic Two crane-downtime requests, alike in every way, got level 1 and level 3

slides.title: Four roles, and the assurer is never the analyst
slides.text: Who does what Four roles, and the assurer is never the analyst Commissioner Asks for the analysis and owns the decision it serves Analyst Does the work and checks it first Assurer Checks it independently, to the level required Approver Signs off that it is fit for its use From the AQuA Book. The UK government's guide to quality analysis (2025 edition) names these four roles and requires the assurer to be independent of the analyst; the degree of separation grows with the importance of the output.

slides.title: Assurance grows with the effect of an error and the complexity of the work
slides.text: Proportionate Assurance grows with the effect of an error and the complexity of the work effect \ complexity low medium high high 3 3 4 medium 2 2 3 low 1 1 2 The reference matrix of Lab 1.1. Business risk is the effect of an error and its likelihood; complexity raises the likelihood.

slides.title: Each level names who checks, who re-runs and who signs
slides.text: The levels Each level names who checks, who re-runs and who signs Level Assurer Re-run Approver 1 Self-check The analyst, with the checklist By the analyst The requester's manager 2 Peer review Another analyst of the unit By the reviewer A senior analyst 3 Independent review A senior analyst who took no part By the reviewer, from the repository The head of the unit 4 Second opinion A senior analyst and a second reviewer By both Head of unit and requesting director

slides.title: Two uses add a level, whatever the matrix says
slides.text: Escalators Two uses add a level, whatever the matrix says Public release The figure leaves the authority: a bulletin, a ministry indicator, a regulator's return. A published error cannot be quietly corrected. Safety use The result sets safety staffing (pilots on duty), a navigation limit or a safety rule. The effect of an error falls on people, not on a budget. Personal data does not raise the level. It adds a check by the data protection officer before the output leaves the unit.

slides.title: A peer applies your words, not your intentions
slides.text: The test of a standard A peer applies your words, not your intentions 1 · You grade effect, complexity, public, safety for six new requests → 2 · A peer grades the same six, alone, with your definitions → 3 · Compare levels every difference points at a definition What goes wrong. "Medium effect: a moderate impact." Two readers, two levels. Write what an error would change: "an operational decision for a month or more".

slides.title: Six requests the unit received this month
slides.text: The six new requests Six requests the unit received this month Id Request Use N1 Weekly berth occupancy for the terminal planning meeting Planning decision N2 Revenue estimate of a proposed tariff change Board paper N3 Arrival-delay model to allocate marine pilots at night Safety staffing N4 Average cargo dwell for the annual public statistics Public statistic N5 Staff survey summary for human resources Internal note, personal data N6 Evaluation of the berth-allocation pilot: continue or stop Board decision

slides.title: A simple count for a public statistic: which level?
slides.text: Checkpoint A simple count for a public statistic: which level? N4: mean import dwell by quarter, one source, a method the unit runs every month. It goes into the authority's published annual statistics. With the matrix and escalators on the earlier slides, what level? Level 1: the method is simple Level 2: medium effect, low complexity Level 3: level 2 from the matrix, plus one for public release Level 4: anything public gets the highest level

slides.title: Six requests, four levels
slides.text: Lab 1.1 · 25 min Six requests, four levels Read the unit's log of 30 requests, write the assurance matrix with its escalators, grade six new requests by risk and complexity, and compare your levels with a second reviewer's. D1_1_assurance_levels.ipynb Read the log: where errors after release came from 5 min Write the matrix and its escalators 7 min Grade the six new requests 7 min Compare with the second reviewer and tighten one definition 6 min ✱ Stretch: Add the sign-off rules: who may approve at each level

slides.title: A team review checklist
slides.text: Session 2 A team review checklist Adapt a published checklist to the unit's work instead of adopting it whole Write each item as a question answered with evidence Tie each item to the assurance levels, with a privacy and classification check in every level 02

slides.title: Your personal checklist becomes the unit's, tied to the levels
slides.text: From DS-310 Your personal checklist becomes the unit's, tied to the levels In DS-310 Five areas, question fit to communication, scored 0 to 2 by one reviewer on one analysis. Here The same five areas as yes-or-no items with named evidence, each required from a level, used by twelve people the same way. Recap only. How to score one analysis is DS-310's; this session decides what the whole unit checks, and when.

slides.title: REFORMS: 32 items in 8 modules, written for others' work
slides.text: Start from a published checklist REFORMS: 32 items in 8 modules, written for others' work Reporting standards for machine-learning-based science, by a consensus of 19 researchers Modules from study goals and reproducibility to leakage and generalisability Its authors say not every item fits every study: decide which are relevant Adapt, do not adopt Most of the unit's work is counts and comparisons. A checklist of 32 machine-learning items gets skipped on every dashboard request.

slides.title: No REFORMS module covers communication: the unit writes those items
slides.text: Mapping No REFORMS module covers communication: the unit writes those items Data 15 items Method 9 Inference 5 Question fit 3 Communication 0 The 32 REFORMS items by the review area of their module (Lab 1.2, task 1).

slides.title: An item is a yes-or-no question with the evidence that answers it
slides.text: One item An item is a yes-or-no question with the evidence that answers it Weak Usable Is the work reproducible? Does it re-run from the repository, with the lock file and README alone, to the reported numbers? Evidence: the re-run log Are the data good? Are excluded and missing records counted, with the reason for each exclusion? Evidence: a count per step Is the comparison valid? Is the comparison fair: a baseline, a control group, the same period? Evidence: the comparison cell

slides.title: Six items at level 1, eleven from level 2
slides.text: Proportionate again Six items at level 1, eleven from level 2 Level 1 : question, sources, exclusions, fair comparison, numbers match, privacy Level 2 adds: decision rule first, duplicates, re-run, uncertainty, where it does not hold Level 3 adds the model item, when there is a model 12 items in the Lab 1.2 checklist, drawing on 18 of the 32 REFORMS items

slides.title: Nothing leaves the unit before the privacy and classification check
slides.text: Every level Nothing leaves the unit before the privacy and classification check The item Before anything leaves the unit: is it free of personal data, and is its classification marked and respected? Required from level 1: a dashboard leaks as easily as a board paper Classification under the NDMO Data Classification Policy Personal data under the Personal Data Protection Law

slides.title: Which item belongs in every level?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which item belongs in every level? Your checklist must stay short at level 1, the self-check that most dashboard requests get. Which of these items is required from level 1? The output is free of personal data and its classification is marked The model is tested on data it never saw A reviewer re-runs it from the repository Every number has an interval

slides.title: A checklist adapted from REFORMS
slides.text: Lab 1.2 · 25 min A checklist adapted from REFORMS Draft a checklist from question to conclusion by adapting a published reproducibility checklist (REFORMS, 32 items): keep, rewrite or drop each item, add the privacy and classification check, and set the level at which each item applies. D1_2_team_checklist.ipynb Map the 32 items to the five review areas 6 min Keep, rewrite or drop each item 8 min Add the privacy and classification item 4 min Set the level of each item and test the length 7 min ✱ Stretch: Add one item for work an assistant drafted

slides.title: Reproducibility as a team rule
slides.text: Session 3 Reproducibility as a team rule Re-run an analysis from its repository before reading its conclusions Classify reproduction failures by kind Write repository rules that make a re-run routine 03

slides.title: From level 2, the reviewer re-runs the analysis before reading it
slides.text: A team rule From level 2, the reviewer re-runs the analysis before reading it 1 · Clone the repository, nothing else → 2 · Follow the README exactly as written → 3 · Log each failure, its kind, the fix → 4 · Compare the figure with the report Recap from DS-310. Re-run first, so the prose does not set your expectations. Here it becomes a rule with a log as its evidence.

slides.title: Saleh's repository, as he sent it
slides.text: Lab 1.3 Saleh's repository, as he sent it README.md dwell.py requirements.txt pandas report.md 4.60 days data/ containers_q3.csv Saleh is a senior analyst; the figure goes in the quarterly note The README says: put containers.csv in data/, install, run Nothing is wrong that Saleh would notice: it runs on his laptop

slides.title: Five failures before the script ran to the end
slides.text: The re-run log Five failures before the script ran to the end # What failed Kind 1 A path to a folder on Saleh's own computer path 2 README names containers.csv; the file is containers_q3.csv documentation 3 berth_lookup.csv is read but not in the repository missing input 4 DataFrame.append is gone in pandas 2; no version pinned library version 5 Two runs, two figures: an unseeded sample of 2,000 randomness

slides.title: It ran, and gave 5.18 days against the reported 4.60
slides.text: The sixth failure It ran, and gave 5.18 days against the reported 4.60 imports = boxes[boxes.move_type != "export"] The filter keeps transshipment with imports The report removed transshipment by hand, in a spreadsheet No file records that step: only the gap shows it Filter on imports in code: 4.60, reproduced What goes wrong. The manual step is the dangerous one: no error, a plausible number, and a reviewer who reads before re-running never sees it.

slides.title: One repository rule for each kind of failure
slides.text: Rules from the log One repository rule for each kind of failure Paths and inputs Relative paths only; every input in the repository or named with its owner Environment A lock file (uv.lock) and the one command that installs from it Determinism A fixed seed in code; no step outside the code

slides.title: A re-run is the cheapest check that finds the most expensive errors
slides.text: The cost A re-run is the cheapest check that finds the most expensive errors With the rules followed, a re-run is one command and a comparison Without them, it is the 25 minutes of Lab 1.3 The rules move the cost from the reviewer to the analyst, where it is smallest Your call as head of unit A repository that does not re-run goes back to its analyst before the review starts. The review clock starts when it runs.

slides.title: Which failure is most dangerous to the unit?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which failure is most dangerous to the unit? A re-run of a colleague's repository meets four problems. Which one most threatens the quality of what the unit releases? The script crashes on a missing file An old library call fails with an error The README names the wrong file A step done by hand that no file records

slides.title: Re-run Saleh's repository
slides.text: Lab 1.3 · 25 min Re-run Saleh's repository Re-run a colleague's cargo-dwell analysis from its repository, record every step that failed and its kind, and reproduce the reported figure. D1_3_rerun_repository.ipynb Follow the README exactly 5 min Log each failure with its kind 8 min Fix a copy until it runs 7 min Reproduce the reported figure or explain the gap 5 min ✱ Stretch: Write the repository rule that would have prevented each failure

slides.title: Rules for AI-assisted analysis
slides.text: Session 4 Rules for AI-assisted analysis Turn the national generative AI guidelines into rules for analytical work Specify the process evidence each analyst keeps Test a rule set on real cases before adopting it 04

slides.title: When an assistant drafts the analysis, the analyst's duty does not move
slides.text: Why rules now When an assistant drafts the analysis, the analyst's duty does not move Musawwada drafts code, numbers and summaries in seconds A fluent draft looks reviewed; it is not The national guidelines put the duty to verify on the user What a unit needs Rules an analyst can follow before the deadline and a reviewer can check from the files.

slides.title: Five duties the unit's rules must carry
slides.text: The national guidelines Five duties the unit's rules must carry Duty, in our words Where Check generated content for accuracy before it is used 3.2 Reliability and Safety Tell recipients when content was created with generative AI 3.3 Transparency and Interpretability Enter no data classified restricted or higher; public data only 3.5 Privacy and Security Keep a clear record of an analysis done with generative AI Practical guidelines: analysing data Verify outputs and generated code before use Appendix 2: checklist

slides.title: Verify, disclose, keep, and what data may go in
slides.text: The rule set Verify, disclose, keep, and what data may go in Verify Re-run every assisted number in your own code before it enters a draft Disclose A line on the deliverable: which tool, which parts, who verified Keep Prompts, outputs and a verification record in the repository Data Public or anonymised data only, approved tools only

slides.title: A rule a reviewer cannot check from the files is a wish
slides.text: Checkable A rule a reviewer cannot check from the files is a wish A wish A rule Use the assistant responsibly Re-run every number it produced, in your own code, before it enters a draft Be transparent about AI use Every deliverable with assisted content carries a disclosure line: tool, parts, verifier Protect sensitive data where possible Only public or anonymised data goes to a hosted assistant

slides.title: Eight scenarios from the unit decide whether the rules work
slides.text: Test before adopting Eight scenarios from the unit decide whether the rules work Allowed Explaining an error message; the approved tool on public statistics, prompts kept Needs action Code checked by hand but no record kept; an analyst who never works unaided Breach A pilot roster pasted in; no disclosure on a board paper; an unchecked 18%; an unapproved tool

slides.title: Who cannot do the work unaided cannot tell when the draft is wrong
slides.text: Keeping the skill Who cannot do the work unaided cannot tell when the draft is wrong Verification needs the skill the assistant replaces One analysis a quarter without an assistant, reviewed like any other The supervised check of this course is AI-off for the same reason Day 2. The same idea returns in development plans: every plan keeps unaided practice in the work.

slides.title: An approved assistant and a restricted file
slides.text: Checkpoint An approved assistant and a restricted file An analyst pastes the night pilot roster, with pilots' names and shifts, into the authority's approved hosted assistant to find fatigue risks. She plans to disclose it and re-run every number. Under the rules, what is it? Allowed: the tool is approved A breach: restricted data may not go to the assistant Allowed once the deliverable is disclosed Needs action: re-run the numbers first

slides.title: Rules for assisted work
slides.text: Lab 1.4 · 25 min Rules for assisted work Write what analysts must verify, disclose and keep as evidence when an assistant drafts work, on one page, and test the rules on eight scenarios from the unit. D1_4_ai_rules.ipynb Read the guideline duties 5 min Write the verify, disclose and keep rules 9 min Decide eight scenarios with your rules 7 min Cut the rules to one page 4 min ✱ Stretch: Add the unaided-practice rule: work each analyst still does without the assistant

slides.title: Three things to keep
slides.text: Day 1 · wrap-up Three things to keep Proportionate The level comes from the effect of an error and the complexity, with written definitions a peer applies the same way. Re-run first From level 2 the reviewer re-runs from the repository and logs every failure; the log writes the repository rules. Checkable rules Assisted work is verified, disclosed and kept, and only public data goes to an assistant.

slides.title: Day 2: Review and develop
slides.text: Next Day 2: Review and develop Tomorrow's first review is AI-off: you form your own judgement before you compare it with a colleague's. Bring your Day 1 standard and checklist; the labs also supply reference versions.

slides.title: Review and develop
slides.text: SDAIA Academy · Leading Analytical Work: Review, Standards and Stakeholders Review and develop Day 2: Calibrated reviewers, audits of assisted work, feedback and a review rota Data Science Track3 teaching days + capstone day4 sessions · 4 labsDS-407

slides.text: Today Review and develop Session 1 · Calibrating reviewers Severity by effect on the decision, rated alone, then compared and turned into clearer wording Session 2 · Auditing assisted work An audit checks the evidence a rule asks for, recomputes what it can and records each breach with its rule Session 3 · Feedback that builds skill From findings to feedback that names the reasoning, and a plan that keeps unaided practice in the work Session 4 · Review capacity and mentoring Review hours follow assurance levels; senior reviewers are the bottleneck; pairings develop analysts

slides.title: Which request is graded right under yesterday's standard?
slides.text: Review of Day 1 Which request is graded right under yesterday's standard? Four requests and the level an analyst gave each, with the unit's matrix and escalators. Which one is graded right? A model that sets night pilot numbers: level 2, it is a simple regression A staff survey summary with personal data: level 3 A dwell figure for the ministry's indicators: level 2 A tariff revenue estimate for the board: level 3

slides.title: Calibrating reviewers
slides.text: Session 1 Calibrating reviewers Rate review findings by their effect on the decision Measure agreement between two reviewers, beyond chance Turn disagreements into clearer checklist wording 01

slides.title: "Slot booking has halved waiting at T2. Extend it to all terminals."
slides.text: The draft "Slot booking has halved waiting at T2. Extend it to all terminals." mean wait, months 13 to 24: T2 7.5 h, other terminals 12.9 h reduction at T2: 42% T2 before 10.7 h, after 7.5 h The berth-allocation pilot: slot booking at T2 from month 13 The director of marine operations wants it extended Two reviewers review it alone: you and Faleh Al-Musharraf

slides.title: Rate a finding by what it does to the decision, not by how you found it
slides.text: Severity Rate a finding by what it does to the decision, not by how you found it 3 · Critical The decision changes, or the output cannot leave the unit 2 · Major The size or the confidence of the result changes, not the decision 1 · Minor Presentation: a label, a chart, a name Recap from DS-310. Ranking flaws by consequence is the individual reviewer's skill. Today two reviewers must reach the same rating, and the unit's standard (S-5) writes the scale down.

slides.title: Six findings, two of them critical
slides.text: The reference review Six findings, two of them critical Finding Severity C1 · T2 compared with others after the change only; T2 was already fastest 3 P1 · Vessel masters' names and mobile numbers in table 5 3 C2 · Diverted calls dropped; at T2 they rose from 17 to 35 2 M1 · "Halved" in the text; 42% in the output 2 M2 · Weather closures in T2's before period 1 m1 · Table 4 labelled minutes; the values are hours 1

slides.title: Fix a flaw and re-run: the decision flips on C1
slides.text: Measuring the effect Fix a flaw and re-run: the decision flips on C1 As written -5.36 h C1 fixed -1.37 h C1 and C2 fixed -0.94 h C1, C2 and M2 fixed -0.78 h Effect of slot booking on waiting at T2, hours per call (Lab 2.1 stretch). The draft recommends extending at -2 hours or more; after C1 it does not.

slides.title: Review alone, then compare, then discuss only the big gaps
slides.text: The method Review alone, then compare, then discuss only the big gaps 1 · Alone re-run, list findings, rate, AI-off → 2 · Compare one table, both ratings, the gap → 3 · Discuss gaps of two levels only → 4 · Revise the checklist sentence that allowed the gap

slides.title: Half the ratings agree; the biggest gap is the privacy finding
slides.text: Two reviewers Half the ratings agree; the biggest gap is the privacy finding Finding You Faleh Gap C1 3 3 0 C2 2 3 1 M1 2 2 0 M2 1 2 1 P1 3 1 2 m1 1 1 0

slides.title: 50% agreement is a weighted kappa of 0.25
slides.text: Beyond chance 50% agreement is a weighted kappa of 0.25 0.25 weighted kappa, six findings (Lab 2.1) Kappa removes the agreement two reviewers reach by chance Weighted kappa counts a gap of two as worse than a gap of one 1 is perfect agreement; 0 is no better than chance Track it each quarter on a shared analysis

slides.title: Each big gap becomes a sentence in the checklist
slides.text: The output of calibration Each big gap becomes a sentence in the checklist P1, before Is the output free of personal data, and is its classification marked? P1, after The same question, plus the anchor: a breach is critical whatever its effect on the decision, because the output cannot leave the unit.

slides.title: High agreement, low kappa: what happened?
slides.text: Checkpoint High agreement, low kappa: what happened? Two reviewers rate 20 findings and agree on 16 of them, 80%. Their weighted kappa is 0.3. Which explanation fits? The kappa was computed wrongly Most findings were rated minor by both, so much of the agreement was expected by chance Four disagreements are too many for any team Twenty findings are too few to compute kappa

slides.title: Two reviewers, one analysis
slides.text: Lab 2.1 · 25 min Two reviewers, one analysis Review a seeded-flaw berth-delay analysis independently with a partner (AI-off), compare severity ratings in an agreement table, and revise the checklist where you disagree. D2_1_calibrate_reviewers.ipynb Re-run and review alone 9 min Rate each finding by its effect on the decision 5 min Agreement table and weighted kappa 6 min Revise the checklist where you disagreed 5 min ✱ Stretch: Measure what each flaw does to the headline by fixing it alone

slides.title: Auditing assisted work
slides.text: Session 2 Auditing assisted work Audit work against rules from its evidence, not its claims Recompute a number an assistant drafted Record each breach with the rule it breaks 02

slides.title: A review asks if the analysis is right; an audit asks if the rules were followed
slides.text: Audit or review A review asks if the analysis is right; an audit asks if the rules were followed Review One analysis, all five areas, before release. The reviewer re-runs and rates findings. Audit A sample of released work, against the rules for assisted analysis. The auditor checks the evidence each rule asks for. The rule of thumb. No evidence, no compliance. "I checked the numbers" is a claim; a verification record is evidence.

slides.title: Five assisted analyses from the unit's log
slides.text: The sample Five assisted analyses from the unit's log Id Analysis What the record shows A1 Tug fuel use per call Disclosed, prompts kept, figures re-run A2 Fatigue risk in the night pilot roster Data sent: names and shifts of pilots A3 Share of T1 calls waiting over 12 hours 18.4%; no verification record A4 Storage-fee scenarios for the board No disclosure line on the paper A5 Gate no-show patterns No prompts, no record; "I checked"

slides.title: A3 says 18.4%; the authority's own data say 47.7%
slides.text: Recompute what you can A3 says 18.4%; the authority's own data say 47.7% t1 = calls[(calls.terminal == "T1") & (calls.month >= 13)] recorded = t1.dropna(subset=["wait_h"]) (recorded.wait_h > 12).mean() # 0.477 1,387 calls with a recorded wait; 35 diverted The record showed the number was not verified Only the recomputation showed how wrong it was

slides.title: Each breach is recorded with the rule it breaks and the action it needs
slides.text: The audit table Each breach is recorded with the rule it breaks and the action it needs Id Rules Action A1 none none A2 C1 data Tell the data protection officer; redo on anonymised data A3 V1 verify, K2 keep Withdraw the figure; re-run and re-review A4 D1 disclose Disclosure note to the board secretary A5 K1, K2 keep Re-run and keep the record before reuse

slides.title: Two of five had no verification record: change the process, not just the analyses
slides.text: What the audit teaches Two of five had no verification record: change the process, not just the analyses The rule existed; nothing made it visible before review Proposed: no review of assisted work starts without its verification record The checklist item C2 asks for it at every level How often Five analyses a quarter, chosen at random from the assisted log, plus any the reviewers flag.

slides.title: An audit finds breaches of rules, not bad analysts
slides.text: Tone An audit finds breaches of rules, not bad analysts Record facts What the file shows, which rule, which action Fix the process Two missing records point at the process, not two people Feed development A pattern for one analyst goes into feedback, the next session

slides.title: "I checked the numbers"
slides.text: Checkpoint "I checked the numbers" An analyst's assisted analysis has a disclosure line and correct figures when you recompute them, but no prompts and no verification record. He says he checked everything. What does the audit record? No breach: the figures are right A breach of the disclosure rule A breach of the keep rules: no prompts and no record A breach of the verify rule only

slides.title: Audit five assisted analyses
slides.text: Lab 2.2 · 25 min Audit five assisted analyses Check five assistant-drafted analyses from the unit's log against the rules for AI-assisted work, recompute the one headline that can be recomputed, and record each breach with its rule. D2_2_audit_assisted.ipynb Read the rules and the log 4 min Check each record against the rules 9 min Recompute one headline number 7 min Write the audit table 5 min ✱ Stretch: Propose the one rule change the audit suggests

slides.title: Feedback that builds skill
slides.text: Session 3 Feedback that builds skill Choose the findings worth raising with an analyst Write feedback that names the reasoning, not only the error Plan development with goals, evidence and unaided practice 03

slides.title: Seven findings is a review; three is feedback
slides.text: From review to feedback Seven findings is a review; three is feedback Shaden Al-Ruwayshid joined six months ago; Faleh found seven things in her notebook The review notes go to the analysis; the feedback goes to the analyst Choose the three findings that show a pattern in her reasoning Name one strength, specifically Her three No comparison group (F2), the wrong population in an average (F1), assisted cells not verified (F7)

slides.title: Observation, effect, reasoning, next step
slides.text: One note Observation, effect, reasoning, next step Part Shaden, F2 Observation In cell 5 waiting at T2 is compared before and after, with no other terminal Effect Waiting fell everywhere in month 13, so most of the fall would have happened anyway Reasoning Before claiming a cause, ask what would have happened without it Next In your next comparison, write the comparison group in the first cell

slides.title: "Be more careful with comparisons" tells her nothing she can do
slides.text: Specific "Be more careful with comparisons" tells her nothing she can do Vague Be more careful. Improve your rigour. Pay attention to the data. Good job on the charts. Specific Cell 3 averages imports with transshipment, 5.2 days. Print the counts by move type before every average. The peer test. Would a colleague reading the note know what Shaden should do differently next week? That is the evidence of outcome 4.

slides.title: Her lowest skills are methods, inference and checking assisted work
slides.text: The plan starts from the profile Her lowest skills are methods, inference and checking assisted work Communication 3 Framing 2 Data handling 2 Reproducibility 2 Methods 1 Inference 1 Assisted-work verification 1 Shaden's skills profile, 1 to 4 (synthetic, Lab 2.3).

slides.title: Three months, each with a goal, the evidence and the support
slides.text: The plan Three months, each with a goal, the evidence and the support Month Goal Evidence 1 A comparison group every time Two analyses passed on checklist item M1 2 Verify every assisted number before review Three complete verification records 3 State uncertainty, working unaided An unaided analysis that passes level 2 review

slides.title: An analyst who checks assistants must still do the work alone
slides.text: Keeping the skill An analyst who checks assistants must still do the work alone Her verification skill is 1 of 4: she cannot check what she cannot do Month 3 is unaided: no assistant, the full analysis, a normal review The rule set's U1 makes this a quarterly habit for everyone From the catalog. Keeping unaided practice in the work is a topic of this course, not an option.

slides.title: Which note will change what she does next week?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which note will change what she does next week? Four feedback notes on the same finding: an average that mixed imports with transshipment. Cell 3 averages imports with transshipment (5.2 days); print counts by move type before every average Be more careful with the populations you average over Your dwell figure was wrong because of transshipment Read the unit's data-handling guide again this month

slides.title: Feedback and a three-month plan
slides.text: Lab 2.3 · 25 min Feedback and a three-month plan Turn review findings on a new analyst's notebook into a feedback note that names the reasoning, and a three-month plan built on her skills profile. D2_3_feedback_plan.ipynb Choose three findings to raise 5 min Write each note: observation, effect, reasoning, next step 9 min A three-month plan from the skills profile 8 min Check that every line is specific 3 min ✱ Stretch: Write the two-line summary for the analyst's file

slides.title: Review capacity and mentoring
slides.text: Session 4 Review capacity and mentoring Estimate a quarter's review hours from assurance levels Assign reviewers under separation and seniority rules Use review pairings to develop analysts 04

slides.title: Assurance levels turn into review hours
slides.text: Capacity Assurance levels turn into review hours Level Analyses next quarter Hours each Who 1 10 0 the analyst 2 14 4 any non-junior peer 3 12 10 a senior 4 4 16 + 8 a senior and a second reviewer

slides.title: Seniors are needed for 184 hours and have 150
slides.text: The bottleneck Seniors are needed for 184 hours and have 150 34 h short in senior review hours next quarter Three seniors, 60, 50 and 40 review hours Six mid-level analysts have hours to spare The rule keeps level 3 and 4 with seniors

slides.title: Close the gap without lowering a level
slides.text: Options Close the gap without lowering a level Co-sign A mid-level analyst reviews a level 3 analysis; a senior checks the review in 2 hours. Saves 8 senior hours. Defer Move a level 3 analysis whose decision can wait to the next quarter, with the sponsor's agreement. Never Lower the level to fit the rota. The level comes from the risk, not the hours.

slides.title: Every rule kept: Faleh and Saleh end at full capacity
slides.text: The rota Every rule kept: Faleh and Saleh end at full capacity Faleh (senior) 60 of 60 h Saleh (senior) 50 of 50 h Noor (senior) 34 of 40 h Lina (mid) 32 of 70 h Rakan (mid) 32 of 70 h Review load from the reference rota of Lab 2.4; five co-signed level 3 reviews.

slides.title: Juniors shadow a mentor's reviews before they review
slides.text: Mentoring Juniors shadow a mentor's reviews before they review Juniors do not review alone, but they watch reviews from their first month One junior per mentor; the mentor reviews some of the junior's work when the rota allows Shaden with Faleh; Turki with Lina; Dalia with Rakan A trade-off to state Faleh is at full capacity and mentors Shaden. Either the shadowing fits inside his reviews, or one of his reviews moves.

slides.title: Senior hours run short: what do you do?
slides.text: Checkpoint Senior hours run short: what do you do? Next quarter's level 3 and 4 reviews need 184 senior hours; your seniors have 150. A director asks you to "just call some of them level 2". Lower five level 3 analyses to level 2 Ask the seniors to absorb the extra hours Let mid-level analysts review level 3 alone Co-sign five level 3 reviews and defer what can wait

slides.title: Three things to keep
slides.text: Day 2 · wrap-up Three things to keep Calibrate Review alone, compare, and turn each big gap into a sentence of the checklist. Audit evidence No record, no compliance; recompute the headline where the record is missing. Develop people Three findings with their reasoning, a plan with evidence and unaided practice, and a rota that trains.

slides.title: Work with sponsors
slides.text: Today Work with sponsors Session 1 · Scope and deadline What can be answered by the deadline, offered as options and recorded when the constraints change Session 2 · Agreeing the evidence first The decision rule and an evidence threshold the data can detect, written and signed before the analysis Session 3 · Pressure on a finding Challenge or pressure: check the finding, weigh the options, decide and record the reasons Session 4 · Reporting quality and correcting errors A quality statement says what was checked, by whom and what is uncertain; a correction says what changed, fast

slides.title: Two reviewers agree on half their ratings. What comes next?
slides.text: Review of Day 2 Two reviewers agree on half their ratings. What comes next? You and a colleague reviewed the same analysis alone. You agree on three of six severity ratings; the largest gap, two levels, is on a privacy finding. Record a severity of 2 for the privacy finding Use the senior reviewer's ratings Discuss the privacy gap and add the sentence to the checklist that prevents it Discuss all three disagreements in turn

slides.title: Scope and deadline
slides.text: Session 1 Scope and deadline Size questions against a deadline, review time included Offer options when a request cannot be met as asked Record what was agreed and what was not 01

slides.title: "I need the slot-booking result for the board in a week"
slides.text: The request "I need the slot-booking result for the board in a week" Bader Al-Khayyal, director of marine operations, sponsors the berth-allocation pilot One analyst is free; the board papers close in five working days The draft he has seen says waiting "halved"; he has heard it has problems The trap Say yes to everything and cut the review, or say no and lose the sponsor. Both are avoidable.

slides.title: The review is part of the time, not something after it
slides.text: Size it first The review is part of the time, not something after it Question Level Analyst days With review Q-a · Waiting at T2 against the other terminals 3 1.5 2.5 Q-b · The same by vessel type, feeders separate 3 0.5 1.5 Q-c · Diversions by terminal 2 1 1.5 Q-d · Forecast for all four terminals 4 6 8 Q-e · Cost to the shipping lines 3 4 5

slides.title: Ask four things before offering anything
slides.text: The meeting Ask four things before offering anything Decision Which decision will this inform, and who takes it? Deadline When exactly, and is there time after it for a correction? Evidence What would convince you, and what would make others object? What exists Is there a draft, an earlier report, a number already quoted?

slides.title: Two options fit five days; the full set needs a later board
slides.text: Options, not refusal Two options fit five days; the full set needs a later board A · 4.0 days Q-a and Q-c: the effect and diversions. Leaves out vessel types, the forecast and the cost to the lines. B · 4.0 days Q-a and Q-b: the effect and vessel types. Leaves out diversions, the forecast and the cost. C · 10.5 days Q-a, Q-b, Q-c, Q-e. Leaves out the forecast; goes to the following board.

slides.title: "Four days, not five. And the deputy CEO wants the feeder lines."
slides.text: Halfway through "Four days, not five. And the deputy CEO wants the feeder lines." Do not Promise the same scope in fewer days. The day that disappears is the review. Do Go back to the options: B fits four days and answers the feeder question. Diversions move to the next board.

slides.title: The scope agreement records what is out as clearly as what is in
slides.text: Write it down The scope agreement records what is out as clearly as what is in Field Recorded Decision Whether to extend slot booking to all four terminals next quarter In scope Q-a, Q-b · 4.0 of 4 working days Out of scope Q-c and Q-e for the following board; Q-d not before a decision to extend After the change Option B: answers the feeder question; diversions move

slides.title: Five criteria, each scored 0 to 2
slides.text: The observer Five criteria, each scored 0 to 2 Asked before offering Offered options, not a refusal The agreed scope fits the deadline Named what is out of scope Handled the change with an option For the observer. Write down the sentence that earned or lost each point. A score without the sentence teaches nothing.

slides.title: The deadline moves from five days to four
slides.text: Checkpoint The deadline moves from five days to four You agreed option A, 4.0 days with review. The sponsor now says four days, and adds a question on feeder vessels. What do you answer? Keep A and add the feeder question; the team will work longer Offer B in place of A: it fits four days and answers the feeder question Drop the review to level 2 so everything fits Say the deadline cannot be met and ask for a later board

slides.title: Agreeing the evidence first
slides.text: Session 2 Agreeing the evidence first Write the decision rule before the analysis Check an evidence threshold against what the data can detect Record roles and sign-off in the agreement 02

slides.title: Agree what result would change the decision before anyone sees it
slides.text: Before the analysis Agree what result would change the decision before anyone sees it After the result, every threshold looks negotiable Before it, the sponsor says what matters to him The agreement turns "extend it if waiting falls" into a rule with numbers From DS-310. Pre-registering a decision rule for your own analysis is the analyst's habit. Here the head of unit agrees it with the sponsor and signs it.

slides.title: Five parts, one page
slides.text: The agreement Five parts, one page Question as the board's choice → Options including not to act → Rule threshold and conditions → Data window and exclusions → Roles level and sign-off

slides.title: With 12 months after the change, the data can detect 0.66 hours
slides.text: What the data can detect With 12 months after the change, the data can detect 0.66 hours 3 months after 1.13 h 6 months after 0.84 h 12 months after 0.66 h Threshold 2.0 h Minimum detectable change of the difference in differences, about 2.8 standard errors (80% power, 5% test). Lab 3.2, synthetic berth calls.

slides.title: Extend only if waiting falls by 2 hours and no vessel type loses more than 2
slides.text: The rule Extend only if waiting falls by 2 hours and no vessel type loses more than 2 Before "Extend it if waiting falls at all." Agreed Extend if waiting at T2 falls by at least 2.0 hours per call against the other terminals, and no vessel type waits more than 2.0 hours longer; otherwise keep at T2 and fix the slots for the type that lost.

slides.title: Level 3: three different people analyse, assure and approve
slides.text: Sign-off Level 3: three different people analyse, assure and approve Role Person Commissioner Bader Al-Khayyal, director of marine operations Analyst Saleh Al-Ghamlas Assurer Faleh Al-Musharraf Approver Arjwan Al-Huqail, head of the unit

slides.title: Waiting fell 0.78 hours; feeders wait 6.32 hours longer
slides.text: Then, the result Waiting fell 0.78 hours; feeders wait 6.32 hours longer -0.78 h all calls at T2, against the other terminals +6.32 h feeder vessels -2.88 h the other vessel types Difference in differences, Lab 3.2 and 3.3, synthetic. Both conditions of the rule fail: keep at T2, fix the feeder slots.

slides.title: A threshold the data cannot test
slides.text: Checkpoint A threshold the data cannot test With three months of data after the change, the minimum detectable change is 1.13 hours. The sponsor wants to extend "if waiting falls by half an hour". What do you do? Sign it: the sponsor sets the threshold Use a looser test so half an hour can show Run the analysis first, then agree the threshold Show him the detectable change and agree a longer window or a threshold the data can test

slides.title: An analysis agreement
slides.text: Lab 3.2 · 25 min An analysis agreement Write an analysis agreement for the pilot decision: question, decision rule and an evidence threshold the data can detect, with roles and sign-off. D3_2_analysis_agreement.ipynb The decision and its options 5 min Compute the change the data can detect 8 min Set the decision rule and the threshold 7 min Roles, level and sign-off 5 min ✱ Stretch: Say in the agreement what happens when the result falls between the thresholds

slides.title: Pressure on a finding
slides.text: Session 3 Pressure on a finding Tell a legitimate challenge from pressure to suppress Respond with options that keep the finding Record a decision with its reasons and references 03

slides.title: "Please take the feeder table out of the paper"
slides.text: The request "Please take the feeder table out of the paper" Khaled Al-Kharji, deputy chief executive for commercial affairs Feeders are "small local operators, less than a quarter of calls" "The table will distract the board"; his team will handle the feeder lines He needs the final version by the end of tomorrow Read it fairly The request is polite and gives reasons. Some of them could be right. Check before you decide.

slides.title: Is it a challenge to the finding, or pressure on it?
slides.text: The first question Is it a challenge to the finding, or pressure on it? A challenge Says the finding may be wrong: too few cases, noise, a coding error. Answered by checking, and the finding may change. Pressure Accepts the finding but wants it unseen: "distracting", "handled elsewhere". Answered by a decision, recorded.

slides.title: 278 feeder calls at T2 after the change: not noise
slides.text: Check it 278 feeder calls at T2 after the change: not noise U.subgroup_did("feeder") # +6.32 h U.subgroup_did(exclude="feeder") # -2.88 h # feeder calls at T2 after: 278, diverted 33 Hundreds of calls; the effect is many times its noise 33 of the 35 diverted T2 calls after the change were feeders The feeder condition is in the signed rule

slides.title: Remove, keep, or keep with context
slides.text: Options Remove, keep, or keep with context Option What it does Remove the table The board may extend a scheme that adds hours of waiting for local lines; the signed rule is not applied Keep it as it is The rule is applied; the commercial team may feel ambushed Keep it with context State the feeder share of calls and revenue; invite the commercial team's plan for the feeder slots

slides.title: Record the decision the same day, with its reasons and references
slides.text: The record Record the decision the same day, with its reasons and references S-7. Findings are not removed from a paper after review; a disagreement is recorded beside the finding S-8. Pressure on a finding is recorded the same day; if repeated, escalated to the chief executive's office The signed rule includes the vessel-type condition SDAIA AI Ethics Principles Fairness · Transparency & Explainability · Accountability & Responsibility

slides.title: Keep the relationship and the finding
slides.text: The reply Keep the relationship and the finding Acknowledge the concern, in his words → Decide the table stays → Why the signed rule, the size → Offer context and his team's plan

slides.title: A senior asks to remove an unfavourable subgroup
slides.text: Checkpoint A senior asks to remove an unfavourable subgroup You checked the subgroup: hundreds of cases, a large effect, and its condition is in the signed decision rule. The deputy chief executive asks again to remove it. What do you do? Remove it and mention it in a footnote Remove it, since he outranks you Keep it, record the repeated request and escalate with the record Keep it, but leave the request out of the record

slides.title: Reporting quality and correcting errors
slides.text: Session 4 Reporting quality and correcting errors Write a quality statement a board can read Correct a released figure quickly and openly Link a correction to the change in process 04

slides.title: A quality statement a board reads in a minute
slides.text: For the board A quality statement a board reads in a minute Part Slot-booking paper Level 3: independent review, approved by the head of unit Checked Re-run to the same figures; every number traced; no personal data By whom Saleh Al-Ghamlas; reviewed by Faleh Al-Musharraf; approved by Arjwan Al-Huqail Uncertain The fall is 0.78 hours per call, likely between 0.3 and 1.3 Assisted Method draft written with the approved assistant, verified line by line Classification Internal

slides.title: "Results may vary" cannot be weighed; "between 0.3 and 1.3 hours" can
slides.text: Uncertainty "Results may vary" cannot be weighed; "between 0.3 and 1.3 hours" can Vague The results are subject to some uncertainty and should be interpreted with care. Usable The fall is likely between 0.3 and 1.3 hours, below the 2-hour threshold agreed with the sponsor.

slides.title: Q2 dwell was released as 4.07 days; it is 4.32
slides.text: After release Q2 dwell was released as 4.07 days; it is 4.32 1,080 rows loaded twice, weeks 5 and 6 The terminal system re-sent two weeks; the load accepted them The duplicated weeks had short dwell, so the mean was understated The figure went to the board and to the ministry's indicator team

slides.title: A correction names the process, not the person
slides.text: The notice A correction names the process, not the person Released and corrected values, side by side The cause in the process: a load that accepted duplicates, a check that did not exist Decisions affected: quoted in the storage-fee discussion; no fee changed on it The change: a duplicate check on every extract, from level 1 for published figures Who is told: the board secretary, the ministry team, the quarterly note's readers S-10. Within five working days of finding the error.

slides.title: Tell the people who acted on the figure before the people who read it
slides.text: Order matters Tell the people who acted on the figure before the people who read it 1 · Board secretary the paper of record quoted it → 2 · Ministry team it went into a national indicator → 3 · Note readers internal readers

slides.title: The corrected figure is better news
slides.text: Checkpoint The corrected figure is better news A released figure is found to be wrong; the corrected value is higher and more favourable to the authority. No decision changed on the old one. What do you do? Use the corrected figure from now on, without a notice Issue a notice within five working days, with both values and the cause in the process Correct it in next quarter's paper Issue a notice naming the analyst who released it

slides.text: Lab 3.4 · 25 min A quality statement and a correction Draft a board-paper quality statement for the pilot evaluation (what was checked, by whom, what remains uncertain) and a correction notice for the Q2 cargo-dwell figure found wrong after release. D3_4_quality_correction.ipynb Write the quality statement 8 min Find and size the Q2 error 7 min Write the correction notice 7 min Check both against the standard 3 min ✱ Stretch: Decide who is told of the correction, and in which order

slides.title: Four documents and their commit history, in a public repository
slides.text: The repository Four documents and their commit history, in a public repository standard.md The level of this analysis: effect, complexity, escalators, and the roles review.md The re-run log and the findings, rated by effect on the decision agreement.md Question, options, decision rule, a threshold the data can detect, sign-off quality_statement.md For the board, at most 160 words, with uncertainty as a number

slides.text: Authenticity Each participant assures a variant of the staffing analysis of their own The repository holds one version, for practice The trainer gives you your own variant this morning, with its own data and flaws Your review report is matched against your variant's key As in Lab 2.1 The same severity scale, the same method: re-run first, then rate by what each finding does to the decision.
